exercises.instructions: Transform the following sentences into double comparatives using 'the + comparative, the + comparative'.

questions.question: When we think of the exam, we get more and more excited. Transform to a double comparative.
options: The more we think of the exam, the more excited we get
The excited we get, the more we think of the exam
We think more of the exam and we get excited
questions.answer: The more we think of the exam, the more excited we get
questions.explanation: Use 'the + comparative' on both sides: 'The more we think..., the more excited we get.' The cause comes first, then the effect. Double comparative မှာ cause ကို ပထမ clause မှာ ထားပါ။

questions.question: As this road gets busier, it becomes more and more dangerous. Transform to a double comparative.
options: The busier this road gets, the more dangerous it becomes
The dangerous it becomes, the busier this road gets
This road gets busy and it becomes dangerous
questions.answer: The busier this road gets, the more dangerous it becomes
questions.explanation: Use 'The busier...the more dangerous'. The cause (busier road) leads to the effect (more dangerous). 'The dangerous' is wrong because it uses positive form instead of comparative. Double comparative မှာ adjective ရဲ့ comparative form ကို သုံးပါ။

questions.question: When you get near to the Equator, the temperature becomes high. Transform to a double comparative.
options: The nearer you get to the Equator, the higher the temperature becomes
The higher the temperature, the nearer you get to the Equator
You get near to the Equator and the temperature is high
questions.answer: The nearer you get to the Equator, the higher the temperature becomes
questions.explanation: Use 'The nearer...the higher'. Getting nearer (cause) leads to higher temperature (effect). Double comparative မှာ cause ကို ပထမ ထားပါ။

questions.question: If she stays in England a long time, her English will be very good. Transform to a double comparative.
options: The longer she stays in England, the better her English will be
The better her English will be, the longer she stays in England
She stays longer in England and her English is good
questions.answer: The longer she stays in England, the better her English will be
questions.explanation: Use 'The longer...the better'. Staying longer (cause) leads to better English (effect). Double comparative မှာ comparative adjective နှစ်ခုလုံး သုံးပါ။

questions.question: When I write fast, my writing becomes illegible. Transform to a double comparative.
options: The faster I write, the more illegible my writing becomes
The illegible my writing becomes, the faster I write
I write fast and my writing is illegible
questions.answer: The faster I write, the more illegible my writing becomes
questions.explanation: Use 'The faster...the more illegible'. Writing faster (cause) leads to more illegible writing (effect). 'More illegible' is the comparative form of 'illegible'. Double comparative မှာ multi-syllable adjective တွေမှာ 'more' သုံးပါ။

questions.question: He got old. He became quiet. Transform to a double comparative.
options: The older he got, the quieter he became
The quieter he became, the older he got
He got old and became quiet
questions.answer: The older he got, the quieter he became
questions.explanation: Use 'The older...the quieter'. Getting older (cause) leads to becoming quieter (effect). Both use comparative forms. Double comparative မှာ short adjective တွေမှာ '-er' suffix ကို သုံးပါ။

questions.question: I waited long. I got angry. Transform to a double comparative.
options: The longer I waited, the angrier I got
The angrier I got, the longer I waited
I waited long and I got angry
questions.answer: The longer I waited, the angrier I got
questions.explanation: Use 'The longer...the angrier'. Waiting longer (cause) leads to getting angrier (effect). 'Angry' becomes 'angrier' in comparative form. Double comparative မှာ comparative form ကို မှန်မှန်ကန်ကန် သုံးပါ။

questions.question: I forget much. I know little. Transform to a double comparative.
options: The more I forget, the less I know
The less I know, the more I forget
I forget much and I know little
questions.answer: The more I forget, the less I know
questions.explanation: Use 'The more...the less'. Forgetting more (cause) leads to knowing less (effect). 'Much' becomes 'more' and 'little' becomes 'less'. Double comparative မှာ 'much' → 'more', 'little' → 'less' ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။

questions.question: As he got older, he became worse tempered. Transform to a double comparative.
options: The older he got, the worse tempered he became
The worse tempered he became, the older he got
He got older and he became worse tempered
questions.answer: The older he got, the worse tempered he became
questions.explanation: Use 'The older...the worse tempered'. Getting older (cause) leads to worse temper (effect). 'Worse' is the comparative of 'bad'. Double comparative မှာ 'bad' → 'worse' ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။

questions.question: You make much money. You spend much. Transform to a double comparative.
options: The more money you make, the more you spend
The more you spend, the more money you make
You make much money and you spend much
questions.answer: The more money you make, the more you spend
questions.explanation: Use 'The more...the more'. Making more money (cause) leads to spending more (effect). Both sides use 'more' as the comparative. Double comparative မှာ cause ကို ပထမ clause မှာ ထားပါ။
